findings.fix: In cmd_ux, hash the shipped /showcase/ files as SERVED by the origin under test, using the isShippedGalleryFile list fetched over HTTP. Require that hash to equal the local hash at the start and at the end of the run. Record the origin and the served hash, and never count a run as a verdict when UX_ORIGIN is set or the hashes differ. Also make server_is_showcase compare the served gallery hash, or at least the served qed64-bridge.js, with the local copy.

findings.issue: `showcase.sh all` can exit 0 after verify has FAILED. cmd_all swallows verify's failure ('continuing: later stages may repair them') but never re-verifies. The script's exit code is then just cmd_ux's rc. This breaks the documented contract 'Exit: 0 ok · 1 a step failed'. The overlay skip also only checks that index.json exists, so a corrupt overlay that verify flags is never rebuilt or re-checked within `all`.
findings.evidence: scripts/showcase.sh:587 `cmd_verify || say "verify reported failures (continuing: later stages may repair them)"`; :593 `SKIP overlay $t` only on `-f …/index.json`; :598-599 `cmd_gallery` then `cmd_ux` with no aggregation of rc. Header :70 says 'Exit: 0 ok · 1 a step failed'. In an APFS clone with tests/experiments/lib.mjs using wasm64-1111111111111111 and widgets8 mathlib.transfer+1, `showcase.sh verify` rc=1 ('FAIL hardcoded buildIds…', 'FAIL overlay widgets8 … size 364676234 != transfer 364676235'). Neither failure is repaired by any later stage of `all` without --rebuild, so all's exit is whatever the UX run returns. I could not run `all` end to end, because the browser is locked by another lane; my attempt to stub the lock for this test was denied. The evidence is the control flow above.
findings.fix: Remember verify's rc in cmd_all, re-run verify after the build stages if it failed, and exit 1 when it is still red, even if ux passes. Alternatively, have the overlay skip require a passing pair-check or cheap overlay check rather than just the existence of index.json.

findings.issue: The headless skip in `all` trusts out/headless/summary.json without checking that it describes the current bakes. summary.json records snapSha256 for every package, but headless_green only compares the runtime and the gate flags. A bake redone in an earlier, separate invocation (e.g. `showcase.sh bake w8`, then `all`) would therefore skip S4 on stale results.
findings.evidence: In a clone I replaced all 15 e1.snapSha256 values in summary.json with 64 zeros (the real value is 84fc22d7…, which equals `shasum -a 256 $W/bake-work-w8/widgets.snap`). `showcase.sh --dry-run all` still printed '[showcase] SKIP headless: out/headless/summary.json (2026-10-01T04:58:14.681Z, wasm64-4b025db7729c5f89) has stage4Green and E2Green'. The code is headless_green at showcase.sh:573-583.
findings.fix: Have headless_green also require that each bake's snapSha256 in summary.json equals the current $W/bake-work-w{7,8}/widgets.snap. A cheaper alternative is to compare the overlay index digest, if summary.json records it.

findings.issue: The UX verdict and the publishing precondition are bound only to the gallery's shipped files. Overlay snapshots, serve.mjs/worker headers and tests/ux are not covered. A rebaked overlay keeps `UX CURRENT` and `G2 … was on THIS gallery`. DEPLOY.md step 2 can then be satisfied for a deploy whose overlays were never UX-tested. Separately, 'full suite' is inferred only from 'no args'. The record keeps no pass/skip counts, and the Playwright config sets no forbidOnly, so a committed test.only or an env-driven skip would still produce a 'full-suite' verdict.
findings.evidence: scripts/lib/gallery-hash.mjs hashes only gallery/ (17 files). In mutation M2 (example source changed), the hash stayed at 2550fa1d… while G1 went red, which shows the hash does not cover the gallery's inputs. In ux_freshness and deploy-manifest galleryGate, green means rc===0 && galleryStart===galleryEnd && !args.length. tests/ux/playwright.config.mjs has no forbidOnly.
findings.fix: Add the lock sha256, the overlay index sha256s and report.json's stats (expected/unexpected/skipped) to the run record. Require them to match the manifest's pin/overlays for G2. Set forbidOnly, or check that the test count equals the expected total.

findings.issue: Some documentation is inaccurate or stale. README Quick start says 'Every one of them was run on 2026-10-01', but the list includes `open http://localhost:5190/showcase/`, which launches a browser in a lane that was not allowed one. The kernel HEAD history in README and the upstream report ends at 3ae65d36, but HEAD is now 6e28e4bd. README says refusals and failures print different lines, but a refused locked step prints both 'probe: FAILED rc=75' and 'REFUSED'.
findings.evidence: `git --no-optional-locks -C wasm64-lean-kernel log --oneline -4` gives 6e28e4bd9d at HEAD, above 3ae65d36f9. `LOCK_WAIT_S=5 showcase.sh locked probe -- bash -c 'exit 3'` printed '[showcase] probe: FAILED rc=75 …' followed by '[showcase] REFUSED: probe: refused by the lock/preflight (rc=75…)', and exited rc=3.
findings.fix: Reword Quick start to say which commands were actually run. Date-stamp the kernel HEAD history or describe it generically. Suppress the FAILED line for rc 75/76/77, or document that both lines appear.
